title: Keeping the best so far
idea: Opener: finding the biggest means remembering ONE 'best so far' and replacing it whenever you meet something bigger. Thinking first.

exercises.prompt: You flip through a stack of photos looking for the tallest building. You keep one 'tallest I've seen so far' in mind. What do you do when a new photo is taller?
options: Replace your 'tallest so far' with the new one
exercises.explanation: You keep ONE best-so-far and swap it out whenever you meet something bigger. That is the whole idea of finding the max.

exercises.prompt: To find the biggest value, you keep a single 'best so far' and update it as you go.
exercises.explanation: One result variable, replaced whenever a bigger value shows up. Same one-result shape as a running total, but you replace instead of add.

exercises.prompt: How is finding the BIGGEST different from TOTALLING a list?
options: Max replaces the best-so-far; a total adds each value in
exercises.explanation: A total adds every value together. Max keeps just one value — the best so far — and replaces it. Different update, same 'one result while walking' shape.

exercises.prompt: Before you look at any value, what is a safe 'best so far' to start with?
options: The first value in the list
exercises.explanation: Start with the first value as your best-so-far, then compare the rest against it. (Starting at 0 would be wrong if every value were negative.)

exercises.prompt: Find the biggest of [4, 9, 2] by hand. Put the 'best so far' after each step in order (start with the first value, 4).
blocks: 9 is bigger than 4, best so far = 9
2 is not bigger than 9, best so far stays 9
exercises.explanation: Start at 4, see 9 (bigger -> 9), see 2 (not bigger -> stays 9). The biggest is 9.
9 beat 4 and 2 never beat 9, so the best-so-far ends at 9.

exercises.prompt: Which real questions are 'find the biggest'? (pick all)
options: What was the hottest day this week?
What is the total of all scores?
exercises.explanation: Hottest day and highest score both ask for the single biggest value. Total is a sum; 'how many' is a count.

exercises.prompt: When you meet a value that is NOT bigger than your best so far, you leave the best so far unchanged.
exercises.explanation: You only replace when the new value wins. Smaller or equal values are ignored, so the best so far holds.

exercises.prompt: You walk [6, 1, 8, 3] keeping the best so far. How many times does the best so far actually CHANGE after the start?
exercises.explanation: Start 6; 1 loses, 8 wins (change!), 3 loses. Only one replacement happens. The best so far ends at 8.

options: Track the best-so-far to find the biggest value in a list
exercises.explanation: Next you'll write the loop that keeps a best-so-far and replaces it with anything bigger.
